title: Does computationally secure public-key encryption exist?
formal: Does there exist a classical public-key encryption scheme with polynomial-time algorithms, negligible correctness error and chosen-plaintext security against probabilistic polynomial-time adversaries, without assuming an unproved hardness conjecture?
context:
This asks about computational security and unconditional existence, not information-theoretic secrecy using only public keys. The implication from one-way functions is separately recorded.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Would establish the existence of secure public communication from a mathematical theorem rather than a computational assumption.
